Build 104: Arabic and Persian drawn right to left, letters joined

RIPPS2 draws text glyph by glyph from the left with no shaping engine, so
Arabic and Persian showed their letters unjoined and backwards. fntsys now
hands any string with right-to-left letters to ripps2Rtl (ripps2tr.c): each
Arabic letter becomes the presentation form its neighbours call for (lam with
alef as one ligature, ZWNJ stopping a join, vowel marks passed over), and
each line is laid out right to left, Latin words and numbers (with their %,
. and :) kept in reading order and brackets turned round. Text is measured
from the same joined letters and wrapped before it is turned, so wrapped
hints read top to bottom.

A mark with no advance that its font draws right of the pen (DejaVu's Arabic
vowel marks, Noto Sans Lao's vowels and tone marks: placed by OpenType, which
fntsys does not read) is now centred over the letter before it, a second mark
above stacking over the first.

The pack carries RIPPS2's own font for Arabic and Persian (DejaVu Sans 2.37
cut to Latin-1, the Arabic block and both presentation-form blocks: upstream's
cut had none of the joined forms) and Noto Sans Lao 2.003 for Laotian, each
with its licence text (elf/lang/fonts, make_lang_fonts.py). Upstream's older
Persian lines were stored pre-joined in an order made for another renderer;
the pack leaves those 248 out and Persian.yml has them written plain.

The joining table is generated from Unicode's data (make_arabic_forms.py).
The build 104 host test checks ripps2Rtl against vectors from a Python twin,
and Lao line breaks (never before a vowel or tone mark of the letter before,
nor after a vowel written ahead of its letter).

VMC: opt-in Rebuild for a card too fragmented for the native core (#986)

An existing card that holds saves but is in too many pieces for native
mcemu (BDM: more than one extent; HDD: PFS map too long) was skipped at
every launch with no way to fix it from the loader. The per-game VMC
dialog now offers Rebuild for exactly that case, after confirmation:

- genvmc gets a copy mode (VMC_CREATE_REBUILD): it creates <name>.new
  exclusively with the same reservation a new card gets (BDM one extent
  via VMC_ALLOC, HDD one PIOCALLOC, refusal = no room), copies every
  byte, reads both back and compares, and on BDM confirms the extent.
  It only accepts a .new target and derives the .bin source itself, so
  it can never write or remove a card; the card is opened read-only.
- The EE (src/vmcrebuild.c) proves .bak/.new absent by reading the
  folder (PFS rename replaces its target), runs the launch's own layout
  check on the copy, then renames card -> .bak and copy -> .bin, undoing
  the first rename if the second fails and syncing PFS after renames.
  Only the copy this rebuild made is ever removed, and only while the
  card is confirmed in place. Card and backup are never deleted.

Host tests: test_vmc_rebuild.py drives the real genvmc and EE code over
an in-memory fs with a fault at every step on BDM and PFS (mutation-
checked); test_vmc_rebuild_fatfs.py fragments a real card on FAT32 and
exFAT images, gets "no room" with nothing changed, then rebuilds it to
one extent with identical bytes and the backup kept across remount.
ZERO hardware testing.

Add compat Mode 8 Slow Reads: Accurate Reads at the CD rate for DVD (#924)

Tales of the Abyss loses its music and SFX after Shurrey Hill and corrupts
SFX boarding the flying ship. Testers on the psx-place OPL thread found it
plays clean at <=1000KB/s and breaks at >=1200KB/s; OPL 0.9's Mode 1
(~900KB/s) fixed it. Our Mode 1 throttles DVD media to 33512 ticks/sector
(~2200KB/s), so it stays too fast.

Honouring the game's requested spindle speed was ruled out: nothing in our
code shows what this title asks for, and changing how sceCdRead's mode is
read would change the read rate of every Mode 1 game that passes a
non-maximum speed.

Mode 8 (OPL core only, greyed under Neutrino) turns Accurate Reads on and
reads DVD media at the CD rate (81920 ticks/sector, ~900KB/s). Mode 1 alone
keeps CD 81920 / DVD 33512, so no other game changes speed. No title
default is added until the reporter confirms on hardware.

COMPAT_MODE_COUNT goes 6 -> 8 so the per-game screen reads and saves bit 7.
That also makes the existing Mode 7 checkbox (Neutrino -gc=7) save: it has
been drawn since rebuild-08 but its bit was dropped on save.

Host test test_accurate_read_rate.py compiles the real rate function and
pins the ticks/sector for CD/DVD with and without Mode 8.

fix(ilink): log back in after an IOP reset; offer only a ready drive (#1018)

i.LINK games listed on every core, Ember booted, and native OPL (PS2
logo, then nothing), Neutrino and POPSTARTER did not. Ember is the only
core that never resets the IOP.

ps2sdk's IEEE1394_bd never logs out (SBP2_LOGOUT_REQUEST is defined but
never sent) and an IOP reset ends it without warning, so the next driver
finds the drive still holding the old exclusive login for its SBP-2
reconnect hold: 2^0 = 1 s for the RECONNECT(0) every login here asks
for, longer on bridges that round it up. It tried 5 LOGINs 200 ms apart
(~0.8 s), inside that hold, and only the next bus reset retries, which a
running game never causes: the device never attached and CDVDMAN waited
forever.

- initConfigureSBP2Device: keep asking every 200 ms for up to 5 s of
  elapsed time (a time budget, so slow refusals cannot stretch it).
- scsi_warmup: TEST UNIT READY at most 300 times, 100 ms apart (30 s for
  a cold 3.5" drive); a block length of 0 is a failure.
- scsi_connect: publish the device only after a successful warm-up; a
  failed attempt frees its slot for the next bus reset.

Vendored as modules/ilink/IEEE1394_bd (ORIGIN.txt: pin, local changes);
the Makefile embeds this build, full or mini, instead of the SDK's.

fix(pops-ilink): log back in after POPSTARTER's IOP reset (#1018)

POPSTARTER resets the IOP and loads its i.LINK driver, usbhdfsd.irx.ilink
(modules/bdmassault/ilink_bd_assault: an older ps2sdk IEEE1394_bd plus
iLinkman), from the memory card. That driver never logs out of the drive
(SBP2_LOGOUT_REQUEST is defined but never sent), so after the reset the
drive still holds the previous driver's exclusive login for its SBP-2
reconnect hold: 1 s for the RECONNECT(0) every login asks for, longer on
bridges that round it up. It tried 5 LOGINs 200 ms apart (~0.8 s),
inside that hold, and only the next bus reset retries, which POPSTARTER
never causes.

Same three changes as OPL's own copy of the driver (PR #1022), with the
same constants and "RiptOPL" markers:

- initConfigureSBP2Device: keep asking every 200 ms for up to 5 s of
  elapsed time (GetSystemTime/SysClock2USec, already imported).
- scsi_warmup: TEST UNIT READY at most 300 times, 100 ms apart; a block
  length of 0 is a failure (the capacity printf divided by it). This
  older driver has no READ CAPACITY(16) path to guard.
- scsi_connect: offer the drive to BDM only after a successful warm-up;
  a failed attempt frees its slot for the next bus reset.

The cdvdman removal and everything else in the driver are unchanged.
test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py compiles the real scsi.c and the login
function against simulated drives and a simulated clock; on the
previous sources it fails 11 checks and crashes on block length 0.

fix(udpfs): deliver the last byte of odd-sized reads (#1010)

smap_fifo_read() copied the PIO tail of a received frame as whole words
and then one u16, with no step for a single last byte. Every odd-length
reply -- the final packet of every odd-sized file read over UDPFS --
came back at the right size with its last byte left as whatever the
buffer held before.

The #1010 tester's Neutrino folder on mc1 shows exactly that: all 29
damaged files have an odd size and differ only in their last byte, and
no even-sized file is touched. The NUL that ended i_dev9_hidden.toml
stops Neutrino with "bad control char in comment" (his udptty log; the
same files fail the same way in Neutrino's own tomlc17 on a PC), so the
UDPFS driver never loads and every game resets to the browser. In
RiptOPL's own menu the lost byte breaks the IEND CRC of odd-sized PNG
covers read over UDPFS.

Read the tail as one whole word (the FIFO pads each frame to 4 bytes)
and store only its valid bytes. Upstream Neutrino master has the same
tail. test_udpfs_smap_fifo_tail.py compiles the real function against a
simulated FIFO and fails on the old code for every odd byte count.

fix(lang): lock the language registry; show English for unsafe translations

Address the CodeRabbit review of #1017.

1. The registry is now a growable array whose entries can be replaced,
   and the IO worker changed it with no lock while the GUI thread read
   it. lngReadEntry grows, fills and replaces a path only under the GUI
   lock (old path freed after), nLanguages is published under it, and
   lngSetGuiValue copies the path under it and reads the file with the
   lock released. Every other reader runs on the IO worker or inside a
   locked GUI frame. The discovery and switch tests now fail on an
   unlocked realloc or a nested lock.

2. The audit checked printf tokens on the fork overlay only, though the
   upstream string wins. Run against upstream today, ten upstream
   strings differ from English, and several would crash: French
   AUTO_START_IN_N_SECS has %s for an int (the Auto Start countdown),
   and three Persian strings swap or add a %s. lngLoadFromFile now
   checks every loaded string (lngFormatFits) and uses the English one
   when its conversions would read other argument types; the same ones
   or fewer in order are kept. The audit checks the merged strings: an
   overlay mismatch fails --strict, an upstream one is a warning, so an
   upstream change cannot break the language build.

games, marked PS1, hashed the way rcheevos hashes a PS1 disc and
launched through POPStarter (krHACKen r13) as mass:/POPS/XX.<name>.ELF.

configuration, the serial and the list in its config block, POPStarter
loads it on the IOP after its own reset. rapops brings up DEV9, SMAP,
the TCP/IP stack and raudp as under a PS2 game, then starts rapull,
which reads the PS1 RAM windows through sceSifGetOtherData at 60 Hz and
hands the snapshots to raudp. The first request waits 25 seconds: one
during POPS's boot leaves the screen black.

BDMAssault pair for the device on the memory card before the launch
(mc?:/POPSTARTER/, RA_BDMA.TXT names the variant): mx4sio, ata, ilink.
USB stays on the built-in FAT32 driver unless "PS1 USB drive is exFAT"
is on in Settings; OPL cannot tell the formats apart, and the usbexfat
pair stalls POPS on its first video from a FAT32 stick.
